messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-sre — high error rate and streaming stalls observed on /v1/stream responses in prod (region: us-west-2). Severity: P1. Initial alert: p95 request latency 3.6s -> 12.4s, p99 9s -> 38s, ~15% of live SSE connections showing stall >10s. related alert IDs: ALERT-STREAM-1768429.

alex: saw the bot. I'm on it. grabbing traces now. any customer reports?

maria: support received 4 tickets, two customers say the stream just hangs after ~10s and client shows no data. They didn't see 502s, just silence.

kevin: I'm tailing proxy logs (stream-proxy-prod-5). seeing repeated: `write: connection timed out` and `client buffer full - applying backpressure` around the same timestamps.

eng-runtime: adding context — we rolled a change to the streaming buffer flush behavior ~40m ago (PR #4521) to improve batching for throughput. Reverting may be an option if it's the cause.

alex: can someone post p95/p99 splits by route? I want streaming vs non-streaming.

sre-bot: metrics snapshot: overall p95 = 3.6s -> 12.4s, p99 = 9.0s -> 38.1s. Streaming route /v1/stream p95 = 6.8s -> 22.9s, p99 = 18.3s -> 76.2s. Non-streaming endpoints unaffected (p95 ~200ms).

kevin: reproduced locally by hitting streaming endpoint behind the proxy with slow-reading client: client read rate ~1kb/s causes server to buffer and then stall; logs show `flush_chunk timeout` followed by `apply_backpressure=true`.

maria: customers report this mostly from browser SSE clients. Could be some intermediary/proxy on client side, but multiple customers in different networks reported it.

alex: priority mitigation ideas: 1) revert PR #4521 to restore previous flush cadence, 2) temporarily reduce max batch size for streaming to 1 token (disable batching) for streaming workers, 3) route streaming traffic to Dedicated pool where buffer/window config differs. Which is fastest?

eng-runtime: quickest is to reduce batch size via runtime flag and restart the streaming worker deployment. Revert PR requires a full service deploy and validation. Routing to Dedicated is slower operationally.

kevin: I'm prepping a `kubectl` restart for stream workers with a lower batch size env: `STREAM_BATCH_TOKENS=8` -> `2`. command ready: ```kubectl set env deploy/stream-workers STREAM_BATCH_TOKENS=2 -n prod && kubectl rollout restart deploy/stream-workers -n prod```

alex: do it. Also open a canary to 10% first.

kevin: doing canary now on three pods. rolling restart started. watching logs.

(5m pass)

kevin: canary pods up. initial check: stream p95 dropped from 22.9s -> 8.2s on canary subset. connections look much healthier, chunk flushes happening more frequently.

maria: customer-facing mitigation: posting to affected customers that we're investigating and routing some traffic to a mitigated path. @support_tina please coordinate messaging.

support_tina: on it — I'll send a terse update: "We’re aware of intermittent streaming stalls for some customers; we’ve deployed a mitigation and will follow up with postmortem."

pm_jordan: need assessment of customer impact window. Alex, can you estimate how many requests affected and which SLAs might be at risk?

alex: based on traffic sampling between 1768429400-1768429800: ~11% of streaming sessions experienced at least one stall >10s. No data loss; just stall. SLA risk: streaming latency SLO p99 30s — we breached it briefly to ~76s. We'll likely need to mark a partial SLO breach for the window ~1768429600-1768430600.

eng-runtime: can we also disable prefix/KV caching for streaming route? Caching interacts with batching and can increase chunk sizes. Quick flag toggle: `DISABLE_STREAM_PREFIX_CACHE=true` on stream-proxy.

kevin: toggled cache off on proxy canary pods and restarted them: logs now show smaller chunk frames, less memory pressure.

alex: monitoring wise — keep eye on p95/p99 for next 30m. Also capture tcpdumps on a few client sessions to confirm it's server-driven buffering, not client network.

kevin: tcpdump on one affected pod attached: saw data queued in kernel socket send buffer and application not flushing due to backpressure. I can share snippet: ```14:12:10.123456 IP pod:: TCP 1000 > 0 bytes queued; socket sendq 16384, rcvq 0```

maria: summarizing visible root cause: new batching/flush behavior + prefix cache interaction created larger chunk windows. Slow-reading clients (SSE in browsers) couldn't keep up, causing server-side backpressure to accumulate and stall streaming flushes. Proxy timeouts not immediate 502s, just silent stalls.

alex: plan: 1) keep reduced batch size and cache disabled for now; 2) patch PR #4521 to add safety guard for slow clients and smaller default flush interval; 3) run load test simulating slow-read clients; 4) revert to original config only after validation. Who owns code fix? eng-runtime + kevin pair.

eng-runtime: will take the patch. target ship in next patch release.

kevin: metrics show recovery: stream p95 now 2.1s on majority of pods, p99 6.4s. Rolling out change to remaining pods.

sre-bot: update: incident severity downgraded to P2. No active customer disconnections reported after mitigation.

support_tina: posting customer update now.

pm_jordan: create postmortem ticket and assign to eng-runtime + kevin + alex. We need clear RCA and action items (code guard, default config change, automated slow-client load test).

alex: created PM-INC-1768429 and linked to this thread. Will add timeline and customer list.

maria: any lasting operational steps? Maybe add an alert rule for streaming stall rate (percent of live SSEs with no chunk for >5s).

eng-runtime: agree — adding an observability metric `streaming.chunk_gap_seconds` and alert if >5s on >3% of streams for 5m.

kevin: rolling final rollout. will keep monitoring for 1h and then hand back to normal oncall.

alex: thanks everyone. handing back to SRE rotation in 60m. If anything pops up ping this thread. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=P2, mitigated=true, postmortem_ticket=PM-INC-1768429. oncall_hand_off_to=oncall-sre-next."
